# `quiz_v1` structure audit — full 56-item display order

**Inspection-only.** Generated by reading `src/core/quiz/bank.ts` (question
definitions, `QUIZ.sections[*].questionIds`, `orderedQuestions()`) and
`src/core/i18n/en.ts` (canonical English copy) directly — no code was changed
to produce this. Display order is `orderedQuestions(QUIZ)`: walk
`quiz.sections` in order, each section's own `questionIds` in order. This is
**not** the order questions appear in the `questions` array literal in
`bank.ts` — that array is authoring order (Phase 0 items first, then Phase 2
and Phase 4 additions appended at the end) and does not match what a user
actually sees. See CLAUDE.md "Phase 6" for why the two orders diverge and why
`orderedQuestions()` exists.

"Bidirectional" / "one-sided" is per CLAUDE.md "Phase 4" / `analyseDirection
Balance()`: a likert item is bidirectional by construction (the 1–7 scale
itself carries the negative pole). A choice item is bidirectional for a
given attribute only if **that specific attribute** appears in two or more
options with **opposite signs** — appearing in only one option, or in
multiple options with the *same* sign, is one-sided for that attribute. Each
item is scored per-attribute-effect below, since a single choice item is
frequently bidirectional for one attribute and one-sided for another.

"Origin" follows the three actual authoring waves: **Phase 0** (original
32-item bank), **Phase 2** (q31/q32, added to fix item-bimodality — see
CLAUDE.md "Known open issues" #2a), **Phase 4** (q33–q56, added across three
rounds to fix one-sided-measurement bias — see CLAUDE.md "Phase 4").

**1. q01** — situational, 4-way
> "You have two free hours and nothing urgent to do. What actually appeals to you most?"
- a. "Follow a question you got curious about down a rabbit hole" → `curiosity` +1 (w1.0), `cross_domain_range` +0.8 (w0.9) — **one-sided**
- b. "Put the time into something you're trying to get good at" → `mastery_orientation` +0.8 (w0.9), `deep_focus` +0.6 (w0.7) — **one-sided**
- c. "Get the week in order so the next few days run smoothly" → `planning_orientation` +1 (w1.0), `detail_orientation` +0.6 (w0.8) — **one-sided**
- d. "Find people and spend the time with them" → `social_assertiveness` +0.8 (w0.9), `collaboration` +0.6 (w0.7) — **one-sided**
- All 8 attribute-effects one-sided (each attribute appears in exactly one option).

**2. q02** — forced_choice, 2-way (rebalanced in Phase 2 — see file header)
> "You have to make a call on something you only half understand. Which is closer to how you get there?"
- a. "Break it down, lay out the evidence, and reason to a conclusion" → `analytical_rigor` +1 (w1.1), `detail_orientation` +0.5 (w0.7), `intuitive_synthesis` −0.5 (w0.7)
- b. "Let it sit, then go with the read that forms on its own" → `intuitive_synthesis` +0.8 (w0.9), `decisiveness` +0.5 (w0.7), `analytical_rigor` −0.3 (w0.5)
- `analytical_rigor`: appears both sides, opposite sign → **bidirectional**
- `intuitive_synthesis`: appears both sides, opposite sign → **bidirectional**
- `detail_orientation`: only in a → **one-sided**
- `decisiveness`: only in b → **one-sided**

**3. q03** — likert7
> "When something goes wrong, I find myself looking for the underlying structure that produced it rather than the immediate cause."
- `systems_abstraction` +1 (w1.1) — bidirectional; `analytical_rigor` +0.4 (w0.6) — bidirectional

**4. q04** — likert7
> "I'll hold a position I've thought through even when most people around me disagree."
- `independent_thinking` +1 (w1.1) — bidirectional; `conflict_tolerance` +0.4 (w0.6) — bidirectional

**5. q05** — situational, 3-way
> "A field you know nothing about turns out to be relevant to your work. What's your first move?"
- a. "Read widely in it for a while before deciding anything" → `curiosity` +0.9 (w1.0), `ambiguity_tolerance` +0.6 (w0.8) — one-sided
- b. "Find the two or three people who know it best and study how they reason" → `analytical_rigor` +0.8 (w0.9), `perfectionism` +0.4 (w0.6) — one-sided
- c. "Try something in it immediately and learn from what breaks" → `execution_speed` +0.9 (w1.0), `decisiveness` +0.7 (w0.8) — one-sided
- All 6 attribute-effects one-sided.

**6. q31** — likert7 (Phase 2 addition, dedicated graded item for `intuitive_synthesis`)
> "When I'm deep in a hard problem, the right next step often occurs to me before I can fully explain why."
- `intuitive_synthesis` +1 (w1.0) — bidirectional

**7. q38** — likert7 (Phase 4 round 1)
> "I'll follow an interesting tangent that has nothing to do with what I'm actually supposed to be doing."
- `curiosity` +1 (w1.0) — bidirectional

**8. q46** — forced_choice, 2-way (Phase 4 round 1, genuine trade-off pair)

- a. "I look for the underlying pattern before the specifics" → `systems_abstraction` +1 (w1.0), `detail_orientation` −0.4 (w0.6)
- b. "I start with concrete examples and build up from there" → `detail_orientation` +1 (w1.0), `systems_abstraction` −0.4 (w0.6)

**9. q53** — likert7 (Phase 4 round 2, added because `analytical_rigor` was still ~27pt above reference after round 1)

## Section-length balance

**Noticeably uneven.** Five of six sections have 8–9 items; Section 3 ("How
You Work") has **12** — 33–50% longer than every other section. This is a
direct, mechanical consequence of `work_style` being the facet Phase 4 added
the most corrective items to (`q34`, `q36`, `q37`, `q47`, `q54`, `q56` — six
of the twenty-plus Phase 4 additions), not a deliberate pacing decision.
Section 3 also sits in the **middle third of the quiz** (positions 18–29 of
56, i.e. roughly the 32%–52% mark) — one of the more common places for
quiz-fatigue drop-off, so the longest section landing there compounds rather
than mitigates that risk.

## Adjacent near-duplicates

**q21 → q39 (positions 34 → 35), immediately adjacent.** Both are likert
items about persisting with an approach versus abandoning it after real
effort is already invested:
- q21: "Once I've committed to something, I'll stay with it well past the
  point where others would switch." (`persistence` +1, `adaptability` −0.3)
- q39: "When new information makes my original approach look wrong, I'll
  drop it and switch, even after I've already put real effort in."
  (`adaptability` +1)

These measure complementary attributes (`persistence` vs. `adaptability`)
and are psychometrically legitimate as a pair, but back-to-back they read as
near-restatements of the same scenario from opposite angles — the strongest
candidate in the whole bank for "this feels repetitive" from a user's seat.

No other strictly-adjacent pair in the 56-item display order shows this
degree of thematic overlap. Situational (3-/4-way) items are never adjacent
to each other anywhere in the bank (good — they're the most cognitively
demanding format, and none of them cluster).

## Non-adjacent near-duplicates (worth knowing, not urgent)

- **q18 (pos 31) / q45 (pos 37), 6 apart.** Both are `risk_tolerance`
  likert items with similar concrete framing: "I'll accept a real chance of
  losing something if the upside is large enough" vs. "I'd rather take a
  shot at something that could fail badly but pay off big, than something
  safe with a modest return."
- **q29 (pos 50) / q42 (pos 53), 3 apart.** Both are `impact_motivation`
  items: "I want the work I do to change something beyond my own
  situation" vs. "Whether my work actually reaches or changes people
  matters more to me than how polished it is on its own terms."

Neither pair is adjacent, so neither reads as back-to-back repetition the
way q21/q39 does — flagged here only because the wording overlap is real,
not because the multi-item-per-attribute design itself is a problem (it
isn't; CLAUDE.md's scoring discipline requires ≥2 independent items per
attribute, approached from different angles, and most pairs in the bank
achieve that cleanly).

## Other UX observations on the current ordering

1. **The quiz opens with its heaviest format.** q01 (position 1) is a
   4-way `situational` choice — the most cognitively demanding item shape
   in the bank — rather than easing in with a likert item. First impression
   is the most complex question, not the simplest.
2. **Phase 4/2 additions cluster at the tail of every section**, since
   `orderedQuestions()` appends each section's later-added items after that
   section's original Phase-0 items (it preserves each section's own
   `questionIds` order, which itself lists Phase 0 items first, then Phase
   2, then Phase 4 — see the arrays above). This means a section's last 2-4
   questions are disproportionately likely to revisit an attribute already
   touched earlier in the same section (e.g. Section 1 opens with curiosity
   via q01 and closes with a dedicated curiosity item, q38, five positions
   later) — not wrong, but a structural pattern worth knowing before any
   reordering work.
3. **Section 6 ends on `mastery_orientation` (q55)**, the same construct
   its own first question (q27, option a) already touched — the quiz's
   very last question circles back to its section's opening theme.
4. **No situational (3-/4-way) items are adjacent to each other** anywhere
   in the 56-item order — already good, worth preserving in any redesign.
5. **Every forced-choice trade-off pair (q36/q40/q46/q47) sits inside a
   run of likert items**, not clustered together — also already good
   variety, worth preserving.
